title: Team session timeline: table-based lanes with time column
description:
## Problem
The team session view renders lanes as independently-scrollable flex columns with full transcript content. This makes it impossible to:
- Follow what happened chronologically across agents
- See when agents were idle vs active
- See inter-agent messages (SendMessage) and their relationships
- Scroll horizontally to see all lanes (columns stack vertically due to CSS bug)
- Reorder lanes on desktop (drag-and-drop only on mobile tab bar)

With 7+ agents, the view is unusable — 405K px of stacked vertical content with no temporal alignment.

## Solution
Redesign the lanes view as a time-normalized table:
- **Sticky time column** (wall-clock + session-relative offset) on left
- **Agent lanes as table columns** (min 280px, max 420px, resizable)
- **Normalized rows** by timestamp — merge messages across lanes into time-aligned rows
- **Collapsed messages by default** (header: role, duration, tool badges, ~80 char preview)
- **Expandable messages** inline (row height adjusts to tallest cell)
- **Explicit idle periods** rendered as stippled/hatched rows with duration
- **Inter-agent message badges** (→ target on sender, ← source on receiver)
- **Hover connectors** SVG overlay lines between sender/receiver turns
- **Click drawer** message content preview + "jump to response" link
- **Drag-and-drop lane reordering** via column headers (phx-hook)
- **Horizontal scroll** with sticky time column and header row
- **Column order** persisted in localStorage keyed to session ID

## Rabbit Holes
- Proportional time zoom (time axis scaled by real duration) — defer, use row-per-event first
- Live session streaming — existing view is static post-hoc, keep it that way
- SVG connector persistence (permanent lines clutter) — hover-only first iteration

## No-gos
- No schema migrations — all changes in compute/render layer
- No authentication/authorization changes
- No changes to transcript import/storage pipeline
- No changes to the single-session (non-team) list view

---
Rig: spotter. Appetite: reviewed.
Target: lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex, lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex, lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex, assets/js/hooks/.
Architecture: Ash + Phoenix LiveView + xterm.js. Sources: CLAUDE.md, navigator scan, architect triage reports.

title: Backend: idle period detection in ParallelLanes
description:
## Why this task is needed now
The table redesign requires idle period data per lane to render stippled/hatched idle rows. Currently `build_lane/2` does not compute gaps between consecutive messages.

## Output files (exact paths)
- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex` — add idle period computation to `build_lane/2`
- `test/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes_test.exs` — 2 failing tests already exist

## Technical specs
- In `build_lane/2`, after sorting messages by timestamp, iterate consecutive pairs
- If gap between `msg_n.timestamp` and `msg_n+1.timestamp` exceeds threshold (default 60 seconds), emit an idle period
- Idle period struct: `%{start: DateTime, end: DateTime, duration_seconds: integer}`
- Add `:idle_periods` key to the lane map returned by `build_lane/2`
- Threshold should be a module attribute `@idle_threshold_seconds 60` for easy tuning

## Component/module usage
- `Spotter.Transcripts.ParallelLanes.build_lane/2` — implementation target
- `Spotter.Transcripts.Message` — timestamp field

## Source references
- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:177` (build_lane/2)
- `test/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes_test.exs` — 2 failing tests at bottom of file

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Lane with 0 or 1 messages → `idle_periods: []`
- Messages with nil timestamps → skip pair
- Very long idle periods (hours) → still emit single period, no splitting

## Architecture constraints
- No schema changes. Pure compute function.
- Must not break existing 21 passing tests.

## Telemetry requirements

title: Backend: row normalization — time-aligned cross-lane rows
description:
## Why this task is needed now
The table redesign requires all lane messages merged into time-aligned rows so the UI can render a synchronized table grid. Currently each lane has an independent message list with no cross-lane alignment.

## Output files (exact paths)
- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex` — add row normalization to `compute/1`
- `test/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes_test.exs` — 2 failing tests already exist

## Technical specs
- After building all lanes (with idle periods and message links), merge all messages from all lanes into a single sorted timeline
- For each message, create a row entry: `%{timestamp: DateTime, cells: %{agent_name => message_or_nil}}`
- Messages from the same lane at very close timestamps (within 1 second) should be grouped into the same row
- Lanes without a message at a given timestamp get `nil` in their cell
- Idle periods should also generate rows: `%{timestamp: DateTime, type: :idle, cells: %{agent_name => %{idle_duration: seconds} | nil}}`
- Add `:rows` key to the result map returned by `compute/1`
- Rows must be sorted by timestamp ascending

## Component/module usage
- `Spotter.Transcripts.ParallelLanes.compute/1` — implementation target
- All lane data from `build_lane/2` — messages with timestamps

## Source references
- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:15` (compute/1)
- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:177` (build_lane/2 — source of lane messages)
- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:228` (compute_timeline/1 — existing time range)
- `test/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes_test.exs` — 2 failing tests at bottom of file

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Empty lanes → no cells for that agent in any row
- All lanes idle at same time → single idle row with all agents marked idle
- Messages with identical timestamps across lanes → same row, different cells
- Very large sessions (1000+ messages) → ensure O(n log n) merge sort, not O(n²)

## Architecture constraints
- No schema changes. Pure compute function.
- Must not break existing 21 passing tests.
- Row normalization depends on idle period computation (task dependency).

title: Frontend: table layout with sticky time column and collapsed messages
description:
## Why this task is needed now
The core UI component needs to be rewritten from flex columns to a time-normalized table grid. This is the main frontend deliverable — it consumes the backend row data and renders the table with sticky axes and collapsed/expandable messages.

## Output files (exact paths)
- `lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex` — full rewrite of lanes_panel, lane_column, lane_header
- `lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex` — new assigns (rows, timeline, overlaps, message_links, expand state), new events
- `priv/static/assets/spotter.css` — new table layout CSS (~200 lines)
- `test/spotter_web/components/lanes_components_test.exs` — updated tests
- `test/spotter_web/live/session_live_lanes_test.exs` — updated tests

## Technical specs
### Table structure
- Outer container: CSS Grid or HTML table with `position: relative`
- Time column: `position: sticky; left: 0; z-index: 10` — shows wall-clock timestamp + session-relative offset
- Agent header row: `position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 9` — agent name, colored dot, stats
- Each row corresponds to a normalized timestamp from backend `rows` data
- Horizontal scroll on the grid container with gradient fade indicators on edges

### Collapsed message headers (default state)
- Role icon (colored dot tied to agent accent color) + role name (user/assistant) in muted text
- Duration: formatted as 2s/45s/2m 14s. Color: green ≤10s, amber ≤60s, red >60s
- Tool badges: small pills for each tool type [Bash] [Read] [Write]. >3 tools → [5 tools]
- Content preview: first ~80 chars, truncated with ellipsis
- Entire row clickable to expand (chevron ▶ closed, ▼ open)

### Expanded messages
- Inline expansion within the cell, row height adjusts to tallest cell
- Full markdown/code rendering (reuse existing TranscriptComponents renderer)
- Tool calls paired with results visually
- Collapsed header sticky at top of expanded cell during vertical scroll
- Click header or [x] to collapse

### Idle period rows
- Stippled/hatched fill in agent's accent color at 15-20% opacity
- Duration label inside when row is tall enough
- Collapsible: thin band with duration + [−] control

### Inter-agent message badges
- Sender turns: `→ recipient` badge in recipient's accent color
- Receiver turns: `← sender` badge in sender's accent color
- Always visible on collapsed headers

### LiveView events
- `toggle_message_expand` — expand/collapse individual messages
- `collapse_all` / `expand_all` — bulk operations
- `collapse_idle` — collapse idle period rows

## Component/module usage
- `SpotterWeb.LanesComponents` — main component module (rewrite)
- `SpotterWeb.TranscriptComponents` — reuse for expanded message rendering
- `SpotterWeb.SessionLive` — event handlers and assigns

## Source references
- `lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex` (current: 157 lines)
- `lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex:231-305` (view mode, load_lanes_data)
- `lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex:498-661` (render)
- `lib/spotter_web/components/transcript_components.ex` (reuse for expanded)
- `priv/static/assets/spotter.css:3886-4020` (current lanes CSS)
- Design spec: frontend-design consultation wireframe

## Edge cases and failure handling
- 0 lanes → show empty state message
- 1 lane → render as single-column table (no horizontal scroll needed)
- Very long expanded messages → max-height with internal scroll per cell
- Many idle periods → bulk collapse affordance

## Architecture constraints
- Phoenix LiveView with server-rendered HTML (no SPA)
- CSS Grid preferred over HTML table for sticky positioning flexibility
- Reuse existing TranscriptComponents for expanded message rendering
- Preserve existing responsive breakpoints (mobile tab bar <1199px)

## Telemetry requirements

- Attributes: `lane_count`, `row_count`, `expanded_count`

title: Frontend: drag-and-drop lane reordering on desktop
description:
## Why this task is needed now
Lane reordering currently only works on the mobile tab bar (LaneDrag hook + SortableJS). Desktop users cannot reorder lanes. The table redesign needs column-header-based drag-and-drop.

## Output files (exact paths)
- `assets/js/hooks/sortable_columns.js` — new JS hook replacing lane_drag.js for desktop
- `lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex` — add phx-hook="SortableColumns" to column headers
- `lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex` — reuse existing `reorder_lanes` event handler
- `priv/static/assets/spotter.css` — drag ghost, insertion line, transition styles

## Technical specs
### Interaction pattern
- Drag handle: grip icon (⠿) on column header hover, `cursor: grab`
- Drag start: ghost copy at 60% opacity, 1.03x scale, drop shadow. Original shows dashed placeholder.
- Drag over: 3px accent insertion line between columns (150ms ease-out animation). No live reorder during drag.
- Drop: column slides to new position (200ms ease-in-out). All columns shift simultaneously.
- Cancel (Escape/off-screen): ghost snaps back (150ms spring).

### JS hook: SortableColumns
- Client-side hook (`phx-hook="SortableColumns"`) managing pointer events
- On drop: push `reorder_lanes` event with new session_id order (reuses existing handler)
- Store column order in `localStorage` keyed to session ID
- On mount: check localStorage for saved order, apply if present
- "Reset column order" button in session toolbar

### Accessibility
- Column header context menu: "Move left", "Move right", "Move to beginning", "Move to end"
- Same animation as drop for menu-based reorder
- Keyboard: focus column header, arrow keys to move

## Component/module usage
- New: `SortableColumns` JS hook
- `SpotterWeb.LanesComponents` — hook attachment on column headers
- `SpotterWeb.SessionLive.handle_event("reorder_lanes")` — existing, reuse as-is

## Source references
- `assets/js/hooks/lane_drag.js` — current tab-bar drag (SortableJS)
- `assets/js/app.js:533` — hook registration
- `lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex:259-287` — reorder_lanes handler
- `lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:34-35` — current LaneDrag hook

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Single lane: disable drag (no reorder possible)
- Drag during scroll: coordinate drag position with scroll offset
- localStorage unavailable: fall back to server order, no error

## Architecture constraints
- Pure client-side JS for drag UX, server event only on drop
- SortableJS library already available (used by LaneDrag)
- Must not conflict with horizontal scroll on the grid container

## Telemetry requirements
- None (client-side interaction, existing server event has telemetry)

title: Frontend: inter-agent message hover connectors and click drawer
description:
## Why this task is needed now
After badges are rendered (in the table layout task), users need to explore inter-agent message relationships. Hover connectors show the visual link; click drawer shows content without scrolling.

## Output files (exact paths)
- `assets/js/hooks/connector_overlay.js` — new JS hook for SVG connector lines on hover
- `assets/js/hooks/message_drawer.js` — new JS hook for click-to-open content drawer
- `lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex` — hook attachment, drawer template
- `priv/static/assets/spotter.css` — connector line styles, drawer styles

## Technical specs
### Hover connectors (Tier 2)
- SVG overlay layer on top of the table (absolute positioned, pointer-events: none except on badges)
- On hover of inter-agent badge: draw horizontal line from sender cell to receiver cell
- Line uses sender's accent color, arrowhead at receiver end
- If receiver turn off-screen: floating indicator at column header "↓ response at +12:30"
- Receiver turn highlighted simultaneously

### Click drawer (Tier 3)
- Click badge → compact drawer opens below sending turn
- Shows: message content preview, sender, recipient, timestamp
- "Jump to response" link scrolls viewport to receiving turn
- Click outside or [x] closes drawer

## Component/module usage
- New: `ConnectorOverlay` JS hook
- New: `MessageDrawer` JS hook
- `SpotterWeb.LanesComponents` — template additions for drawer and SVG layer
- Backend `message_links` data from ParallelLanes.compute/1

- `lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex` — message_links data structure
- Design spec: 3-tier inter-agent message visualization

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Badge hover while scrolling: debounce connector render (100ms)
- Receiver in collapsed idle block: expand idle block first, then highlight
- Multiple outgoing messages in same turn: show all connectors simultaneously
- SVG overlay resize: recalculate on window resize and column reorder

## Architecture constraints
- SVG overlay must not intercept pointer events for table cells
- Connectors are ephemeral (hover-only), not persisted
- Must work with horizontal scroll (connector coordinates relative to scroll position)

title: Team session rendering and import improvements
description:
## Problem
Team sessions imported into Spotter have multiple rendering and UX deficiencies:
1. No auto-import of sister sessions with the same teamName — each team member must be imported individually
2. Timeline entries overlap in lanes view — no time-proportional positioning
3. Lane columns render raw message data instead of piping through TranscriptRenderer, resulting in missing tool blocks, code blocks, and markdown
4. Lane tab bar lacks drag-and-drop reorder capability
Additionally, teammate-message XML tags in message content are now classified correctly (Bug #4 fix landed) but still need styled rendering in the frontend.

## Solution
1. Add team-aware grouping to transcript discovery and "Import Team" bulk action
2. Render each lane through TranscriptRenderer pipeline for full-fidelity display
3. Fix timeline positioning or switch to independent scrollable panels per lane
4. Add SortableJS-based drag-and-drop to lane tab bar with persisted order

## Rabbit Holes
- Time-proportional timeline layout is complex and may not be the right UX — consider independent scrollable panels instead
- Auto-import could be slow if many team sessions exist — need pagination or lazy loading
- SortableJS dependency weight and LiveView hook integration complexity

## No-gos
- No authentication/authorization changes
- No schema migrations for lane order (use socket assigns only for now)
- No changes to the JSONL parser — team messages use standard types with embedded XML

---
Rig: spotter. Appetite: reviewed.

title: Auto-import sister team sessions
description:
## Why this task is needed now
When importing a team session, users must manually select each team member's JSONL file individually. There is no way to import all team members at once, leading to partial imports and confusion about which sessions belong together.

## Technical specs
- build_preview/3 must include team_name (string | nil) in the returned preview map, extracted from first JSONL line "teamName" field
- Discovery must group previews by team_name so UI can show team clusters

title: Render lanes through TranscriptRenderer pipeline
description:
## Why this task is needed now
Lane columns currently render raw Message data (msg.role + summarize_content) bypassing the TranscriptRenderer pipeline entirely. This means lanes show no tool blocks, no code blocks, no markdown, no styled messages — just plain text summaries. Many entries show blank content. This is the highest visual impact bug.

## Output files
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex (pipe lanes through TranscriptRenderer, use transcript_panel component)

- rendered_lines must include tool_use blocks, code blocks, markdown, teammate-message styled bubbles

title: Fix timeline overlap and lane positioning
description:
## Why this task is needed now
Timeline entries in lanes view overlap visually. The time_axis component renders overlap bars that are disconnected from lane message positions. Messages use flow layout (stacked vertically) with no time-proportional positioning, causing visual confusion. Overlap bars show duplicate timestamps.

## Output files
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex (fix lane positioning — either time-proportional CSS or independent scrollable panels)
- lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex (compute time positions if using proportional layout)
- assets/css/lanes.css or equivalent (positioning styles)
- test/spotter_web/components/lanes_components_test.exs (positioning tests)
- e2e/tests/session-lanes.smoke.spec.ts (visual regression tests)

## Technical specs
- Decision needed: time-proportional positioning vs independent scrollable panels
  - Time-proportional: each message positioned based on timestamp relative to session start/end, gaps between messages visible
  - Independent panels (recommended): each lane is an independent scrollable panel, no time axis needed, simpler implementation
- If independent panels: remove time_axis component from lanes view, each lane scrolls independently
- If time-proportional: compute y-position = (msg.timestamp - session_start) / (session_end - session_start) * container_height

## Component/module usage
- LanesComponents.lane_column/1 — positioning fix
- LanesComponents.time_axis/1 — remove or fix
- ParallelLanes.compute/1 — time position calculation if needed

## Source references
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:101-115 (lane_column flow layout)
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:60-90 (time_axis component)
- lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:46-52 (timeline + overlaps computation)
- docs/design/parallel-transcript-lanes.md (design spec)

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Sessions with very short duration — ensure messages don't collapse to 0-height
- Sessions with long idle periods — avoid huge empty gaps in time-proportional mode
- Single-member "team" sessions — degrade gracefully to single panel

## Architecture constraints
- Must work with LiveView — no heavy client-side JS frameworks
- CSS-only positioning preferred over JS-computed positions
- Must be responsive for different viewport widths

## Telemetry requirements
- N/A — rendering-only change

- [] Tests to verify the behaviour exist or were added, and executed and pass.
- [] Relevant e2e tests were executed and pass.
- [] The changes were reviewed using code-reviewer and coderabbit:code-reviewer.

title: Add drag-and-drop reorder to lane tab bar
description:
## Why this task is needed now
The lane tab bar already exists with click-to-switch functionality, but users cannot reorder lanes by dragging tabs. Reordering should also change the visual order of lane columns. This is a UX feature requested by the user.

## Output files
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex (add phx-hook for drag-and-drop on tab bar)
- assets/js/hooks/lane_drag.js (new JS hook for SortableJS or HTML5 DnD)
- lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex (handle "reorder_lanes" event, update lane_order assign)
- assets/package.json (add sortablejs dependency if using SortableJS)
- test/spotter_web/live/session_live_lanes_test.exs (reorder event tests)

## Technical specs
- Use SortableJS (lightweight, well-maintained) via JS hook
- Hook name: LaneDrag
- On drag end: push "reorder_lanes" event with new order (list of session_ids)
- Server stores lane_order in socket assigns (not persisted to DB)
- Lane columns re-render in new order
- Tab bar reflects new order with animation
- Drag handle: the tab itself (colored dot + agent name)

## Component/module usage
- LanesComponents.lanes_panel/1 — add phx-hook="LaneDrag" to tab bar container
- SessionLive — handle "reorder_lanes" event
- LaneDrag JS hook — initialize SortableJS on mount, push events on drag end

## Source references
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:30-57 (lanes_panel with tab bar)
- lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex:251-258 (switch_lane handler)
- e2e/support/pages/lanes.ts (lanes POM)

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Dragging to same position — no-op
- Single lane — drag disabled
- Lane removed during drag (session deleted) — handle gracefully
- Mobile/touch — SortableJS supports touch events natively

## Architecture constraints
- Must integrate with Phoenix LiveView hooks pattern
- SortableJS must be imported as ES module
- No persistence to DB — session-scoped only (socket assigns)

## Telemetry requirements
- N/A — UI-only feature
